statement: Let n = len(passingFees). A valid journey is a finite sequence of cities c_0, c_1, ..., c_k (k ≥ 0) together with a finite sequence of edges e_0, ..., e_{k-1} such that c_0 = 0, c_k = n - 1, for each i with 0 ≤ i < k the edge e_i is in edges and connects c_i and c_{i+1} (i.e., {edges[e_i][0], edges[e_i][1]} = {c_i, c_{i+1}}), and the total travel time Σ_{i=0}^{k-1} edges[e_i][2] is at most maxTime. The cost of a valid journey is the sum of passingFees[j] over the set of distinct cities j that appear in the sequence c_0, ..., c_k. The function returns a result r such that: if there is no valid journey, then r = -1; if there is at least one valid journey, then r = min{ cost(J) | J is a valid journey } and there exists a valid journey J with cost(J) = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(passingFees) and m = len(edges). The inputs satisfy: 1 ≤ maxTime ≤ 1000; 2 ≤ n ≤ 1000; m ≥ n - 1 and m ≤ 1000; for every j with 0 ≤ j < n, 1 ≤ passingFees[j] ≤ 1000; for every i with 0 ≤ i < m, len(edges[i]) = 3, 0 ≤ edges[i][0] < n, 0 ≤ edges[i][1] < n, edges[i][0] ≠ edges[i][1], and 1 ≤ edges[i][2] ≤ 1000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, there exists an i64 value r such that min_cost maxTime edges passingFees = Result.ok r. In other words, the function never fails, panics, or overflows.

statement: Let n = len(passingFees). If the function returns a result r and r ≠ -1, then there exists a simple path from city 0 to city n-1 with total travel time at most maxTime and cost exactly r. A simple path is a sequence of distinct cities c_0, c_1, ..., c_k with c_0 = 0, c_k = n-1, c_i ≠ c_j for all i ≠ j, and for each i with 0 ≤ i < k there is an edge in edges connecting c_i and c_{i+1}; the cost is the sum of passingFees over these cities, and the total time is the sum of the travel times of chosen edges.

statement: Let n = len(passingFees). Let P be the set of all simple paths from city 0 to city n-1 with total travel time at most maxTime (a simple path is a sequence of distinct cities c_0, ..., c_k with c_0 = 0, c_k = n-1, and for each consecutive pair there is an edge in edges connecting them; the total time is the sum of the travel times of chosen edges, and the cost is the sum of passingFees over the cities in the sequence). If P is empty, the function returns r = -1; otherwise, the function returns r = min{ cost(p) | p ∈ P } and there exists p ∈ P with cost(p) = r.
